problem: Given that the distance from a point $P$ to the origin is $4,$ and that $P$ makes an angle of $\frac{4\pi }{3}$ with the positive $x$-axis, what are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$

feedback.problem:
If the distance from a point $P$ to the origin is $12,$ and that $P$ makes an angle of ${60}^{∘}$ with the positive $x$-axis, then the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are$\,(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We notice that the point $P$ is described using polar coordinates $(r,\theta )$, where

$$
r=12,\,\theta ={60}^{∘}.
$$

To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =12\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡({60}^{∘}) \\  & =12\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =12\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡({60}^{∘}) \\  & =12\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =6\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(6,6\sqrt{3}).$
